blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cape Horn
Debut — 1251 Ghuman Place (Beedie Living)

The first Fraser Mills tower: a 36-storey concrete condo high-rise with 318 homes, approved by Council on September 25 (developer source), on a five-storey podium holding 32 townhomes at the base, on a site preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain. A later developer article records Debut as sold out. Completion timing conflicts between sources: the developer's approval article expected move-in by 2026, current listings record the year built as 2027, and the developer's Chapter article expects Debut, Encore and Chapter all complete by 2028 — completion is UNCONFIRMED until the strata plan registers. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED. REDMA applies to developer contracts.
Encore — 53 Kong Court (Beedie Living)

The second Fraser Mills tower: 32 storeys, 306 homes of condominiums and three-bedroom stacked townhomes, concrete construction, built to Energy Step Code 3, with almost 27,000 sq ft of amenities (developer sources). A presale source states the project is in the Cape Horn district of Coquitlam and expects completion in the summer of 2028; one current listing records the year built as 2029 — the conflict is noted, not resolved. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED. REDMA applies.
Chapter — 58 Kong Street (Beedie Living)

The third Fraser Mills building and the developer's only wood-frame complex on the site: two six-storey low-rises over a shared parkade, 173 suites in total (82 units in the northern building, 91 in the southern), stratified housing, expected complete in 2028 (developer source). A presale-directory record for the same address records 173 units, 6 floors, low-rise form and preconstruction status. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED. REDMA applies.
Streets, schools and getting around Cape Horn

items.t: Cape Horn is the established residential slope in south Coquitlam above the Cape Horn interchange, where Highway 1 (Trans-Canada Highway), Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) meet at the Port Mann Bridge approach; the City tracks the area as planning areas 15 and 16 in its development statistics. No City neighbourhood plan boundary for Cape Horn is stated on a City page in the sources read — the exact boundary is UNVERIFIED; the working description is the slope above the interchange, below Austin Avenue / Mariner Way.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is no completed apartment-condo stock on the slope itself —. The only strata product filed under Cape Horn by listing sources is the Fraser Mills presale site below the slope, on the Fraser River waterfront at United Boulevard & King Edward Street (Debut, Encore and Chapter by Beedie Living), plus one older townhome complex on Cape Horn Avenue itself (Crescentview).
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Coquitlam condos & townhomes median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market).

The City's own permit record underlines the slope's form: the 2022 development statistics for Cape Horn (planning areas 15 and 16) record 18 net residential units created that year (36 created, 18 demolished), all in single-family / secondary-suite / carriage-house form, with no townhouse or apartment units.

Main roads: Mariner Way and Cape Horn Avenue are the residential roads connecting the slope to the interchange; United Boulevard is the light-industrial and commercial road below the slope, and the Fraser Mills site sits at United Boulevard & King Edward Street.
Transit anchors: the nearest SkyTrain stations are Braid, Lougheed Town Centre and Burquitlam — none is inside the sub-area. Bus routes serving Cape Horn's interior streets: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cape Horn

items.t: Floodplain — the Fraser Mills diligence item: the Debut site is preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain — flood construction level, strata insurance and deductible position are first-order questions for every Fraser Mills purchase. On the slope, the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse, and Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks while s.523 covers riparian areas.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cape Horn

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026. The City adopted an Interim Official Community Plan on April 27, 2026, streamlining the old Citywide OCP (Bylaw No. 3479, 2001), with a fuller OCP update anticipated to begin in 2027. Planning documents and listing copy citing the old Citywide OCP designations are already a plan out of date.

The sub-area's attached listings are a construction site, not a resale market. Cape Horn's 13 condos & townhomes listings in September 2026 sit against a City permit record (2022, planning areas 15/16) of zero townhouse or apartment units created — the listings are Fraser Mills presale contracts at three buildings (Debut 318 homes, Encore 306, Chapter 173) that between them will add 797 homes below the slope.

A 12-kilometre water main is being built through the area. Metro Vancouver's Coquitlam Water Main Cape Horn Section is approximately four kilometres long and 2.2 metres in diameter, running to Hickey Drive and Mariner Way, including a trenchless tunnel crossing under Lougheed Highway — construction disruption on the Mariner Way corridor is a live diligence item for slope addresses.

Debut's podium hides the townhouses. Of Debut's 318 strata units, 286 are high-rise apartments and 32 are townhouses inside the five-storey podium — "townhomes at Debut" are podium units in a tower strata, not a townhouse complex.
The interchange is the amenity and the discount at once.

Chapter is marketed to seniors but is not published as 55+. The developer describes Chapter's buyers as families upgrading or seniors downsizing; no age-restriction bylaw is published in the sources checked. In BC only a 55+ bylaw under SPA ss.123.1/123.2 can restrict age — marketing language cannot.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Cape Horn
Plain statement at the top, as required: Cape Horn has ZERO verified completed townhouse complexes — 0 strata, 0 fee-simple.
Streets, schools and getting around Cape Horn

items.t: Where the townhouse-form product actually sits: not on the slope. Crescentview Townhomes stands on Cape Horn Avenue itself, and the Fraser Mills site — Debut, Encore and Chapter by Beedie Living — sits below the slope on the Fraser River waterfront at United Boulevard & King Edward Street, filed under Cape Horn by listing sources.

Schools: School District 43 catchments are address-based, and no Cape Horn address-level catchment is verified — the only locator run in the research used 575 Poirier Street (Coquitlam Public Library Poirier branch), which sits outside Cape Horn and returned Parkland Elementary, École Montgomery Middle and Centennial Secondary for that address only. Run every Cape Horn address in the SD43 locator individually.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cape Horn

items.t: Form B diligence — the position here is inverted, stated plainly: there is no completed strata townhouse complex in Cape Horn, so there is no resale Form B to pull for townhouse stock on the slope. When a strata complex does apply (Strata Property Act s. 59), the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. At Fraser Mills, presale diligence is the developer's disclosure statement, not a Form B — do not let a sales centre present the two as equivalents.

Flood and watercourse — the two diligence items by location: at Fraser Mills, the Debut site is preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain — flood construction level, strata insurance and deductible position are first-order questions for every Fraser Mills purchase. On the slope, the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse, and Zoning Bylaw s. 519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses while s. 523 covers riparian areas; slope/geotechnical status for a specific lot: UNVERIFIED.

Coquitlam property taxes and utilities: property tax payment was due July 2, 2026 for the January 1 – December 31, 2026 year, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance of current taxes after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants). Utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; the City's 2026 budget materials record an average-household total property-charges increase of $137 combined, and metered properties under the Voluntary Residential Water Metering Program are billed every four months instead of the annual flat rate.

Infrastructure note for slope addresses: Metro Vancouver is constructing the Coquitlam Water Main — approximately 12 kilometres in four sections; the Cape Horn Section is approximately four kilometres long and 2.2 metres in diameter, running from Westwood Street and Dewdney Trunk Road to Hickey Drive and Mariner Way, including a trenchless tunnel crossing under Lougheed Highway — construction disruption on the Mariner Way corridor is a live diligence item.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Cape Horn?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 13 condos and townhomes listed in Cape Horn. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Cape Horn a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Cape Horn had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Cape Horn from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 0 condos and townhomes sold in Cape Horn over those 4 months, out of 475 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: Are there any resale condos in Cape Horn?
faq.a: The "Cape Horn" condo listings a portal shows are Fraser Mills presale contracts below the slope.

faq.q: What is Fraser Mills, and is it in Cape Horn?
faq.a: Beedie Living's master-planned waterfront community on the historic Fraser River Sawmill site at United Boulevard & King Edward Street — 96 acres, developed over roughly 25 years, with 16 towers planned in the developer's material.

faq.q: When can I move into Debut, Encore or Chapter?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED as a single date for any of them. Sources conflict: Debut was expected ready by 2026 in the developer's approval article, current listings say 2027, and the developer's Chapter article expects all three buildings complete by 2028; Encore's presale source says summer 2028 while one listing says 2029. The disclosure statement's estimated completion date governs — read it before relying on any year.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Fraser Mills unit long-term?
faq.a: Strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals are a separate question a bylaw can still restrict.

faq.q: Is Chapter an apartment building or townhouses?
faq.a: Neither in the usual sense: Chapter is two six-storey wood-frame low-rise condominium buildings (82 + 91 units, 173 total) over a shared parkade — the only wood-frame project planned at Fraser Mills, per the developer. Debut's 32 podium homes and Encore's stacked homes are the project's townhouse-form product, inside the towers.

faq.q: Are there any towhouses I can buy in Cape Horn today?
faq.a: No completed townhouse complex is verified — the count is zero on both tenures. The "Cape Horn" townhouse-form listings a portal shows are Fraser Mills presale contracts below the slope, plus one rental complex on Cape Horn Avenue.

faq.q: What is Fraser Mills, and is it in Cape Horn?
faq.a: Beedie Living's master-planned waterfront community on the historic Fraser River sawmill site at United Boulevard & King Edward Street, developed over roughly 25 years.

faq.q: Where are the townhouses at Fraser Mills?
faq.a: Inside the towers, not beside them: Debut's five-storey podium holds 32 townhomes at the base of a 36-storey tower (286 of its 318 units are apartments), and Encore's 306 homes mix condominiums with three-bedroom stacked townhomes (the stacked-townhome count is UNCONFIRMED). Chapter is low-rise apartments, not townhouses. All are presale components — none is a standalone townhouse complex.
